draft_passage: For that strange spectacle—the head turned sunwards—conveyed a new wondrousness.
why_damaged: The draft cuts the source's explicit gloss that this sunward-turning is a phenomenon 'observable in all sperm whales dying,' so the reader has no idea whose head is turning or why this is remarkable.
source_context: "that strange spectacle observable in all sperm whales dying—the turning sunwards of the head, and so expiring—that strange spectacle, beheld of such a placid evening, somehow to Ahab conveyed a wondrousness unknown before"

why_damaged: The antecedents for 'that one' and 'this one' were the 'rainbowed jet' and the 'trebly hooped hip of power' which are themselves metaphorical—but the source sentence structure makes clear both refer to the whale's striving upward vs. jetting; without the cut connective tissue the two pronouns are indistinguishable from one another.
source_context: "Oh, trebly hooped and welded hip of power! Oh, high aspiring, rainbowed jet!—that one strivest, this one jettest all in vain!"
